item.research_question: How can the strong immiscibility among repelling elements be overcome to synthesize high-entropy alloy nanoparticles with more than 15 elements for efficient photothermal conversion?
item.material_system: 21-element high-entropy alloy nanoparticles (FeCoNiCrYTiVCuAlNbMoTaWZnCdPbBiAgInMnSn) and series of 9-, 13-, and 17-element HEA-NPs
item.processing_route: Arc-discharged plasma method with extremely high evaporation temperature, ultra-fast cooling (300 K and 150 K), and a vapor-pressure (V.P.) strategy to adjust powder ratios (e.g., 10x Ti/V, 0.5x Cu/Al)
item.test_conditions: Simulated sunlight (1.0 kW m–2 to 5.0 kW m–2), pure water and saline water (3.5 wt% to 10 wt%), outdoor testing at 41.76° N, 123.42° E
key_findings: 21-HEA-NPs achieved an average absorption of >92% across the entire solar spectrum (250 to 2500 nm).
The 21-HEA-NPs reached a solar steam efficiency of nearly 99% under 1 sun irradiation.
The water evaporation rate of 21-HEA-NPs was 2.42 kg m–2 h–1 under 1 sun irradiation.
Mixing entropy (ΔSmix) increased with element count, reaching 24.28 J mol–1 K–1 for 21-HEA-NPs.
Surface temperature of 21-HEA-NPs increased to ~107°C within 90 s under 1 sun irradiation.
Thermal conductivity of 21-HEA-NPs was reduced by >15% compared to 7-HEA-NPs.
In 10 wt% saline water, the evaporation rate stabilized at ~2.36 kg m–2 h–1 and efficiency at 95.52% after 100 h.
Outdoor evaporation rate reached 4.13 kg m–2 h–1 under ~0.80 sun irradiation.
item.mechanism: The enhanced photothermal conversion is attributed to the coupling of reinforced d–d interband transitions (IBTs) due to fully filled energy regions around the Fermi level and the lattice distortion effect (high-entropy induced), which reduces thermal conductivity and promotes heat accumulation.
item.limitations: The text notes that phase separation occurred when elements exceeded eight in previous experiments without the V.P. strategy, and that Sn and In exhibited slightly constituent fluctuation in the 21-HEA-NPs.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the approach opens a vast space for synthesizing ultra-mixing HEA-NPs with immiscible elements, broadening the family of HEA-NPs and providing a platform for exploring unknown properties and various applications.
quotes: Due to the reinforced lattice distortion effect and excellent IBTs, the nanoparticles can realize an average absorption of >92% in the entire solar spectrum (250 to 2500 nm).
In particular, the 21-element nanoparticles achieve a considerably high solar steam efficiency of nearly 99% under one solar irradiation, with a water evaporation rate of 2.42 kg m–2 h–1.

The reduction of thermal conductivity can result in the accumulation of heat under solar irradiation, increasing the surface temperature of nanoparticles and thus enhancing the water evaporation rate.
